description: T06 (design guidelines §3): the Weapon Order step is a side-anchored panel - the B2 shooting resolution dock's ordering step in the right HUD column (it replaced the centred WeaponOrderDialog in single-player) - with Esc to cancel. Fixture shooting_phase, P1 Orks. The Battlewagon Alpha quick-assigns its three guns to the Witchseekers and the player clicks Confirm Targets: the phase waits in awaiting_weapon_order and the dock shows the order (rows with ▲▼, Roll to Hit = Start Sequence, Fast Roll All, Back to Targets (Esc)). Tier A: dock left edge >= 60% of the viewport, its column anchored right, no intersection with the board's on-screen rect, no overlap with the right-side phase controls; pixel_diff of the before/after frames: board_left (left 60%) and the board rect < 1%, right_panel > 10%. The board still answers the mouse (hover forecast over the Witchseekers, no Control hovered). Esc and the Back button return to targeting with the same three assignments and nothing rolled; CONFIRM_TARGETS dispatched succeeds with weapon_order_required. With SMOKE on the Witchseekers (setup privilege), a declined SMOKESCREEN window keeps Back available, a used one locks the targets in (Back greyed, Esc refused with the reason). Roll to Hit then starts the staged sequence with all three weapons, Back goes away, and a mid-roll Esc changes nothing.

steps.comment: Setup: pick the shooter (not the feature under test).
Player path: Quick Assign 'All -> Witchseekers' aims all three guns (big shoota, lobba, zzap gun) - three weapon types, so Confirm leads to the weapon-order step.
Three weapon types declared; the exact declaration is kept for the after-Esc comparison.
Before: no weapon-order surface yet; the camera is recorded so we can prove it does not move.
Player path: Confirm Targets opens the weapon-order step.
Tier A (BEGIN_WEAPON_ORDER equivalent): the click put the phase in awaiting_weapon_order and the right-HUD dock in its ordering step.

Tier B 'all controls the old modal had': one row per weapon naming its target, each with ▲▼ reorder; Start Sequence (Roll to Hit ▶); Fast Roll All; plus the new Back to Targets (Esc) the modal lacked.
Tier A: the panel lives in the right 40% of the screen (left edge / viewport width >= 0.6).

steps.script:
var hr = tree.root.get_node("Main/HUD_Right")
return hr.anchor_left == 1.0 and hr.anchor_right == 1.0 and hr.offset_left < 0.0
steps.comment: Tier A 'anchor right set': the column the panel lives in is anchored to the right edge (anchor_left = anchor_right = 1).
Tier A: the panel's rect does NOT intersect the board's on-screen used rect (SceneRefs.board_screen_rect, the BoardRoot extent through the camera).

Tier B 'no layout overlap with the right-side phase controls': the panel sits inside HUD_Right and overlaps neither the End Phase button, the top bar, the phase strip, the log, nor any other visible widget of the shooting panel.
No centred WeaponOrderDialog window is opened in single-player.
Tier B 'tokens at original positions': the camera did not move when the panel opened.
Tier A: board region (left 60%) unchanged while the panel is open.
The battlefield itself (its on-screen rect) unchanged.
Tier A: the right panel region changed (the weapon-order panel replaced the declaration widgets).
mouse_filter does not cover the board: the board still answers the mouse while the panel is open.

Over the Witchseekers no Control is hovered, and the board's own hover handling draws the shooter-to-target LoS line (T11: BoardRoot/LOSLineVisual, which replaced the controller's plain red ShootingLoSVisual line).
A board click on an enemy while ordering must not re-aim guns behind the panel (the old modal swallowed it).
Nothing re-aimed; the panel tells the player Esc goes back to targets.
... and a click on another friendly unit does not switch shooters mid-activation.

steps.script:
var hov = tree.root.get_viewport().gui_get_hovered_control()
return str(hov.name) if hov != null else "null"
steps.comment: Control: over the panel the panel does take the mouse (the null above is not vacuous).
Tier B: Esc dismisses the panel without committing.

Back to targeting with nothing committed: dock retired, declaration widgets back with the SAME three assignments (weapon > target > bearer), no confirmed shot or resolution state, shooter still selected, unit not shot, no Witchseeker wounded, no settings menu.
After Esc the right panel is the pre-Confirm declaration again.
... and the weapon-order panel is really gone.
Confirm again: the weapon-order step reopens.
The visible Back to Targets (Esc) button does what Esc does.

Back to targeting with nothing committed: dock retired, declaration widgets back with the SAME three assignments (weapon > target > bearer), no confirmed shot or resolution state, shooter still selected, unit not shot, no Witchseeker wounded, no settings menu.
Tier A: the action that begins the weapon order (CONFIRM_TARGETS with 2+ weapon types; the task's BEGIN_WEAPON_ORDER) succeeds and asks for the order.
The dispatched confirm opens the same panel.

Back to targeting with nothing committed: dock retired, declaration widgets back with the SAME three assignments (weapon > target > bearer), no confirmed shot or resolution state, shooter still selected, unit not shot, no Witchseeker wounded, no settings menu.
Setup privilege (precedent iss15_smokescreen_reactive_11e): the Witchseekers get SMOKE so targeting them offers the defender the 11e core SMOKESCREEN.
The defender declines - no reaction.
Declined: the weapon-order step opens.
A declined window is not a reaction: Back is still available.

Back to targeting with nothing committed: dock retired, declaration widgets back with the SAME three assignments (weapon > target > bearer), no confirmed shot or resolution state, shooter still selected, unit not shot, no Witchseeker wounded, no settings menu.
This time the defender reacts: SMOKESCREEN on the Witchseekers (1 CP).
After the reaction the weapon-order step opens.
Locked in: the opponent reacted to these targets, so Back is greyed out and its tooltip says why.
Esc on a locked declaration changes nothing and the panel says why.
Start Sequence: Roll to Hit sends RESOLVE_WEAPON_SEQUENCE with the panel's order, as the old modal's button did.
The sequence runs (staged, all three weapons in order) and the panel's Back is gone once dice roll.
Mid-roll Esc is a no-op: no deselect (the old half-state), no menu.
